editorial:
Ever wondered what birds talk about when they fly over a big city? You get to find out in this charming old documentary. It follows a group of black-headed gulls as they migrate from the North of England all the way down to the busy streets of London. The vibe is very relaxed and curious, making you feel like you are taking a nature walk through the 1930s. It is a sweet, simple look at how animals move through the world and how they interact with the humans living in the city.

What really grabs you is the slow-motion footage of the birds flying, which was pretty impressive for its time. You also get a glimpse into some weird old habits, like people eating gull eggs as a fancy treat. While it is a bit slow by today's standards, it is a great piece of history.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing the harsh reality of nature. You see a polecat eating gull eggs, but then you see humans doing the same thing for food. It explains that thousands of these eggs were sold in London markets back then. The movie ends by letting you listen to the birds' chatter, leaving you to think about the relationship between wildlife and the growing city of London.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves nature and old black and white films.
